terms.comment: One whose counsel is asked, a king’s or a magistrate’s adviser; in Suetonius also an assessor who sits with a judge.

terms.gloss: the one who advises or urges a course
evidence: Cic. Att. 15.5: mihique ut absim, vehementer auctor est (Lewis & Short)
Plaut. Ps. 1.3.2: quid mihi es auctor?
terms.comment: Above all the author, founder or source of a thing; as adviser, in auctor esse (+ dat., ut + subj.): quid mihi es auctor?, what do you advise me?

evidence: Cic. Att. 16.7.2: suāsor et impulsor profectiōnis (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The one who talked someone into a course, often in a bad light.

sources: Lewis & Short: consiliarius · Lewis & Short: auctor · Lewis & Short: suasor
